database_meta.purpose: Maintained catalog of real, current real estate tools to ground the discovery-call-extractor Skill's recommendations in vetted fact rather than model guesswork.

tools.name: Follow Up Boss
tools.use_case: Centralizes leads from Zillow, website, and referrals into one pipeline; automates follow-up sequences and lead routing for teams.
tools.cost: Grow $58/month, Pro $416/month (10 users), Platform $833/month (30 users), Dialer add-on $33/user/month
tools.setup_time: Low for basic pipeline setup (same day); medium (1-2 weeks) for full automation/action-plan configuration and lead-source integrations.
tools.notes: Gold-standard CRM-first hub, deep third-party integrations (250+). No native transaction document management. Best fit when the core pain point is fragmented lead sources plus slow follow-up.

tools.name: Lofty (formerly Chime)
tools.use_case: All-in-one AI-powered CRM bundling lead gen, marketing automation, automated social posting, and an AI assistant that engages leads 24/7.
tools.setup_time: Medium-high given the bundled feature set (CRM + marketing + website).
tools.notes: Best when a client wants to consolidate several tools (CRM, marketing, IDX site) rather than add point solutions.

tools.name: ShowingTime (Appointment Center)
tools.use_case: MLS-integrated showing coordination between listing agent, buyer agent, and seller; automated notifications and feedback collection.
tools.setup_time: Low; largely turnkey once connected to MLS and lockbox systems.
tools.notes: De facto standard where available via MLS (600+ MLS integrations). Does not do post-showing follow-up automation on its own. Pricing is contact-sales based, not published; vendor page confirms this rather than listing numbers.

tools.name: Calendly
tools.use_case: General appointment booking for buyer consultations, listing presentations, and discovery/review calls (not private MLS showings).
tools.cost: Free tier available; paid plans from ~$10/user/month.
tools.notes: Good complement to ShowingTime rather than a replacement; handles the non-showing meeting types.

tools.name: ListedKit
tools.use_case: AI-assisted transaction coordination with pay-per-transaction pricing; contract intake and document/deadline tracking.
tools.setup_time: Low; per-transaction model avoids upfront platform setup.
tools.notes: Good fit for lower or variable transaction volume where a flat monthly TC platform isn't justified yet.

tools.name: DocJacket
tools.use_case: Per-seat transaction coordination with unlimited transactions and AI contract data extraction.
tools.notes: Best team-value option cited for independent TCs; unlimited-transaction pricing suits higher volume than ListedKit's pay-per-intake model.

tools.name: SkySlope
tools.use_case: Compliance-focused transaction management with AI compliance engine covering all 50 states.
tools.setup_time: Medium-high; more configuration for compliance workflows across states.
tools.notes: Best fit for brokerages with multi-state or heavier compliance needs, not solo agents.

tools.name: ListingAI
tools.use_case: Generates MLS-compliant, SEO-optimized listing descriptions plus virtual staging, video, and CMA reports from one platform.
tools.cost: Essential $19/month, Professional $36/month, Expert $150/month, plus Free tier
tools.notes: Broader than pure description writing; worth flagging if a client's pain point spans listing marketing generally, not just text.

tools.name: EstatePass Listing Description Generator
tools.use_case: Free MLS-ready property description generator with fair housing language compliance checks and multiple writing styles.
tools.notes: Good default recommendation for a client where listing descriptions are a minor time cost, not worth a paid tool.

tools.name: Claude (via claude.ai) for listing descriptions
tools.use_case: Draft listing descriptions and multi-platform social captions directly from property details, styled to the agent's voice.
tools.cost: $20/month (Claude Pro), likely already covered if the client has a subscription from other AI-Assisted recommendations.
tools.setup_time: Low; requires a short style/voice calibration but no integration work.
tools.notes: Requires a human read-through for Fair Housing compliance and factual accuracy before publishing, same caveat as any AI-drafted description.

tools.name: Coffee & Contracts
tools.use_case: Done-for-you social media content library: Canva templates, captions, Reels trend briefs for Instagram/Facebook/TikTok.
tools.setup_time: Low; templates are ready to customize, no design work required.
tools.notes: No built-in scheduling/posting automation; still needs a scheduler like Buffer paired with it.

tools.name: Buffer
tools.use_case: Cross-platform social media scheduling and auto-publishing (Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, X, Threads).
tools.cost: Essentials $5/month per channel (yearly), Team $10/month per channel (yearly)
tools.notes: Scheduling only, no content creation. Pairs naturally with Coffee & Contracts or Claude-drafted captions.

tools.name: Structurely
tools.use_case: AI-driven lead nurture via text/voice, trained specifically on real estate buyer/seller conversations; qualifies leads before handoff to a human agent.
tools.setup_time: Medium; needs CRM integration (works with Follow Up Boss and Lofty) and conversation-flow tuning.
tools.notes: Best recommended only when lead volume genuinely justifies the cost; overkill for a 1-3 agent team with low lead flow.

tools.name: Freshchat (Freshworks)
tools.use_case: General-purpose AI chatbot/messaging platform configured for real estate FAQs, lead qualification, and agent handoff across web/mobile/messaging.
tools.setup_time: Medium; requires FAQ/flow training even though it's not real-estate-specific out of the box.
tools.notes: Cheaper general-purpose alternative to Structurely when a client wants basic chat coverage without real-estate-specific training.
